subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency requirements (Finly)
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Kaur <priya.kaur@finly.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — quick notes from today's discovery call

Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick notes from our side so we have alignment before any follow-up: 

- Current stack: Finly's inference lives on a mixed fleet of k8s nodes backed by AWS g4dn/GPU instances. LLMs are run via an internal microservice (predictor) that currently uses model-hosting on single-node VMs.
- Pain points:
  - P95 latency for our conversational flows spikes to ~1.2s under bursty load (expected should be <= 500ms p95).
  - Streaming UX suffers: partial tokens are batched aggressively upstream causing chunked playback and poor perceived latency.
  - Concurrency needs: we expect sustained concurrency ~120 qps for 2 minute windows with 400 qps peaks during settlement runs.
- Success criteria (what would make a POC/rollout a win):
  - Reduce conversational p95 to <= 450–500ms at 120 sustained qps with streaming enabled.
  - Smooth streaming token delivery (no >150ms gaps between first token and subsequent tokens).
  - Predictable per-token cost within 15% of current baseline.

I attached the traffic sample we discussed and can also share an infra diagram if helpful. Interested to see what a POC might look like and rough capacity/cost estimates.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Shah
Head of ML Ops, Finly
Samir Shah <samir.shah@finly.com>

Attachments: finly-traffic-sample.csv (CSV, 120KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick notes from today's discovery call

Samir — great to speak this morning. Appreciate the clear success criteria; below is a concise recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment. I tried to keep this focused on latency/throughput/streaming since that was the primary ask.

Recap of pain points you highlighted:
- p95 spikes to ~1.2s under realistic bursts; target is <= ~450–500ms
- Streaming UX degrades because upstream batching delays first-token delivery and token chunking is visible to end-users
- Need predictable inference costs during concurrency peaks and sustained windows

What we learned about your current environment:
- Mixed k8s + VM fleet on AWS (g4dn family) running an internal predictor service
- Average token lengths for conversational flows: 60–120 tokens; settlement flows can hit 800+ tokens
- Typical session pattern: many short interactive queries (low token counts) plus scheduled heavier jobs causing 4x concurrency spikes

Redwood's initial technical approach (high level):
- Serving: route interactive conversational traffic to a low-latency pool optimized for short sequences (kernel selection + optimized KV cache). Use separate batch-optimized pool for the long settlement jobs.
- Streaming: enable continuous prefix streaming with smaller micro-batches for first-token delivery and progressive token emit to avoid >150ms gaps.
- Autoscaling and routing: policy to keep interactive traffic on dedicated low-latency hosts; fallback to quantized variants for non-critical throughput bursts.

Preliminary P95 targets for POC (what we'll try to achieve in scope):
- 450ms p95 for conversational workload at sustained 120 qps (with streaming on)
- Sub-150ms time-to-first-token for 80% of requests
- Handle short peaks to 400 qps with graceful degradation via model variants / traffic shaping

Data / artifacts requested from Finly (to scope POC accurately):
1) Representative traffic sample (timestamps, tokens per request, streaming vs non-streaming) — you already attached this and that helps a lot.
2) Infra diagram (VPC layout, egress constraints, any KMS/HSM for keys).
3) Example SLA/uptime expectations and cost targets for inference.

Suggested next steps / timeline:
- Week 1: Share infra diagram + any rate-limiting configs (Samir) — for sizing and network checks
- Week 2: Redwood runs sizing exercise + provides POC plan (expected infra, estimated cost, proposed success tests)
- Week 3: Lightweight POC (2 weeks of testing) to validate p95 and streaming UX on customer-like traffic

Attachments: redwood-discovery-recap.pdf (summary of our proposed approach + initial SLOs).

I'll follow up with a short scope doc and a proposed POC statement of work. Looping Aditya for technical planning and Ethan for commercial/ops readiness.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
www.redwood.ai
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick notes from today's discovery call

Samir — quick technical clarifications from my side so we can size the low-latency pool and propose model variants: 

- Can you share a 24-hour traffic sample with request timestamps and token counts (we need distribution not just averages). The earlier CSV is helpful but we need percentiles per minute.
- Are you currently maintaining per-session KV caches or is every request cold? If you have prefix caching client-side, that changes our batch strategy.
- Network constraints: outbound bandwidth limits or strict egress rules? Also let us know if we need to integrate with a customer KMS — that affects deployment mode.

I've attached our inference-runbook-template.docx to show the fields we usually request for POCs (hardware, token budgets, acceptable model variants, test harness). Once we have those, I'll propose concrete sizing for: 
- low-latency GPU count (p95 sizing)
- batch pool params (max batch size, micro-batch window for streaming)

CC Ethan so he can flag any ops/monitoring expectations we need to include.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Attachments: inference-runbook-template.docx (DOCX, 95KB)

Thanks team — yes, getting the 24-hour minute-level sample and infra diagram to you by end of day. A couple quick answers: 
- We currently have largely cold predictor instances for each request; session affinity is limited (we do hold short-lived session IDs client side but we purge caches after 5 minutes).
- No special egress limits but we do have strict outbound IP allowlists — happy to share the list for any POC hosts.
- KMS: yes, we use AWS KMS for keys; any POC will need to integrate with our KMS or run via a dedicated Private deployment (we're open to both).

I'll upload the minute-level traffic CSV and the infra diagram to the Drive link and share the HubSpot deal with more internal context. Looking forward to the sizing note next week.

Best,
Samir
